topics.title: Structure, classification and nomenclature of amines

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the sp3 hybridisation of nitrogen and the pyramidal shape of amines.
Classify amines as primary, secondary or tertiary from the number of groups on nitrogen.
Name alkylamines and arylamines by common and IUPAC systems.
Explain the reduction of nitro compounds to amines and the advantage of iron scrap and HCl.
Explain ammonolysis of alkyl halides and why it gives a mixture of amines.
Apply Gabriel phthalimide synthesis and Hoffmann bromamide degradation to prepare primary amines.
Relate the boiling points of amines to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
Explain the solubility of amines in water in terms of hydrogen bonding and the alkyl part.
Interpret Kb and pKb values to compare the basic strength of amines.
Explain the order of basicity of alkylamines from inductive, solvation and steric effects.
Explain why arylamines are weaker bases than ammonia and how substituents change this.

topics.title: Alkylation, acylation and tests for amines

concepts.learning_objective: Describe acylation and benzoylation of primary and secondary amines.
Use the carbylamine reaction and the reaction with nitrous acid to identify primary amines.
Distinguish primary, secondary and tertiary amines with benzenesulphonyl chloride.
Explain the ortho/para directing and activating effect of the amino group.
Explain how acetylation controls the reactivity of aniline in substitution.
Explain meta product in nitration, sulphonation and failure of Friedel-Crafts reaction of aniline.
Describe the preparation of benzenediazonium chloride by diazotisation.
Explain the stability of arenediazonium salts compared with alkyldiazonium salts.

topics.title: Reactions of diazonium salts and their importance in synthesis

concepts.learning_objective: Describe replacement of the diazonium group by halide, cyanide, hydroxyl, hydrogen and nitro groups.
Describe coupling reactions of diazonium salts with phenol and aniline to form azo compounds.
Plan syntheses of aromatic compounds that cannot be made by direct substitution.
